harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed an inventory web application (Python stdlib HTTP server serving JSON at /inventory and /healthz) as a systemd service (inventory-app) on node2 and node3, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080. Configured nginx on node1 with an upstream block load-balancing port 80 across 10.100.3.11:8080 and 10.100.3.12:8080 via round-robin. Verified even traffic distribution across both backends. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, then node1 (LB), confirming changed boot IDs and full service/LB recovery after each restart while keeping the other backend available throughout.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline state of node1/node2/node3 (Ubuntu 24.04, no pre-existing web services)
Wrote /opt/inventory-app/app.py (stdlib HTTP server with /inventory and /healthz JSON endpoints) on node2 and node3
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service on node2 and node3; verified active and responding on 127.0.0.1:8080
Verified node1 can reach both backends over the cluster network (10.100.3.11:8080, 10.100.3.12:8080)
Installed nginx on node1
Configured /etc/nginx/sites-available/inventory-lb with an upstream block for both backends, listening on port 80, proxying to the upstream group
Enabled the site, removed the default site, validated with nginx -t, reloaded nginx

Verified round-robin load balancing via repeated curl requests (10/10 split across node2/node3 confirmed; noted apparent skew on rapid bursts explained by 4 independent nginx worker round-robin counters)
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service-health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot; confirmed boot_id changed, inventory-app auto-started (enabled), service responded, and it rejoined the LB rotation
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot (node2 kept serving traffic); confirmed boot_id changed, inventory-app auto-started, service responded, rejoined LB rotation
Restarted node1 (the load balancer) last via systemctl reboot; confirmed boot_id changed, nginx auto-started (enabled), and it correctly proxied to node2
Ran a final 10-request distribution check through node1 confirming both node2 and node3 backends are serving traffic post-restart

evidence.requirement: Inventory app running on node2 port 8080
evidence.summary: app.py deployed and inventory-app.service active, curl to 127.0.0.1:8080/inventory returns node2 JSON

evidence.requirement: Inventory app running on node3 port 8080
evidence.summary: app.py deployed and inventory-app.service active, curl to 127.0.0.1:8080/inventory returns node3 JSON

evidence.requirement: node1 load-balances HTTP on port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: nginx installed, upstream config validated and reloaded; spaced requests show clean node2/node3 alternation and a 10/10 split confirming balanced distribution

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 17b362d1..., reboot triggered (stream closed), post-restart boot_id cf564f63... with new uptime, inventory-app active and serving, LB rotation confirmed it rejoined via node1 checks

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c0691b74..., reboot triggered, post-restart boot_id 6844d1d8... with new uptime, inventory-app active and serving; node1 continued serving via node2 during the outage

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b19a635d..., reboot triggered, post-restart boot_id 97bc4d10... with new uptime, nginx active and successfully proxying; final 10-request check shows 6/4 split across both backends confirming full LB recovery
